<a id="Checked"></a>

### The artefacts a shipment ships are checked

`Checked` · `src/obligations.ts:130` · status: **held**

Each check of an artefact the shipment ships is to prove: those a program runs, or all of them.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ counts, every }) => (sketch: GraphSketch, reach: ObligationReach, p: { by: CheckWay }): ObligationFinding => ({
    obliged: once(reach.shipped.flatMap((a) => edgesTo(sketch, a, CheckEdge.on)
      .filter((c) => kindOf(sketch, c) === KindName.check && (p.by === every || counts.any(edgesFrom(sketch, c, CheckEdge.runs))))
      .map((c) => ({ node: c, via: a })))),
    gaps: [],
  })
```

</details>

| Constant | Value | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `every` | `all` | The word of CheckWays that takes every check of the artefacts, those made by hand too |

<a id="Preceded"></a>

### The artefacts a shipment ships were shipped first by those that precede it

`Preceded` · `src/obligations.ts:176` · status: **held**

Each shipment named that ships an artefact this one ships is to prove: it must have shipped that artefact first, the same file, before this one may take it (a public version after its preview, a release after staging). A shipment may wait for several; each artefact waits for every one of them that ships it. An artefact none of them ships is a gap: it would go further without having been anywhere before.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (sketch: GraphSketch, reach: ObligationReach, p: { by: readonly SketchNode[] }): ObligationFinding => {
    const ships = (s: SketchNode, a: string) => edgesFrom(sketch, s.ref, ShipmentEdge.ships).includes(a)
    return {
      obliged: once(reach.shipped.flatMap((a) => p.by.filter((s) => ships(s, a)).map((s) => ({ node: s.ref, via: a })))),
      gaps: reach.shipped.filter((a) => !p.by.some((s) => ships(s, a))),
    }
  }
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [Rules applied, not written again](product.md#SharedRules)

({ counts }) => (sketch: GraphSketch, reach: ObligationReach): ObligationFinding => {
    const datasets = reach.reached.filter((r) => kindOf(sketch, r) === KindName.dataset)

      obliged: once(datasets.flatMap((d) => edgesTo(sketch, d, ReviewEdge.of).filter((v) => kindOf(sketch, v) === KindName.review).map((v) => ({ node: v, via: d })))),
      gaps: datasets.filter((d) => counts.isEmpty(edgesTo(sketch, d, ReviewEdge.of))),
    }
  }

<a id="Served"></a>

### The product a shipment serves holds

`Served` · `src/obligations.ts:48` · status: **held**

From what the shipment reaches, what it serves; from the requirements served, up through what they refine, to the goals. Every requirement that refines those goals or those requirements, at any depth, is to prove.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
() => (sketch: GraphSketch, reach: ObligationReach): ObligationFinding => {
    const up = (from: string, seen = new Set<string>()): Set<string> => {
      for (const to of [...edgesFrom(sketch, from, EdgeName.serves), ...edgesFrom(sketch, from, EdgeName.refines)]) {
        if (seen.has(to)) continue
        seen.add(to)
        up(to, seen)
      }
      return seen
    }
    const down = (to: string, seen = new Set<string>()): Set<string> => {
      for (const from of edgesTo(sketch, to, EdgeName.refines)) {
        if (seen.has(from)) continue
        seen.add(from)
        down(from, seen)
      }
      return seen
    }
    return {
      obliged: once(reach.reached.flatMap((r) => {
        const served = [...up(r)]
        return [...new Set([...served, ...served.flatMap((s) => [...down(s)])])]
          .filter((n) => kindOf(sketch, n) === KindName.requirement)
          .map((n) => ({ node: n, via: r }))
      })),
      gaps: [],
    }
  }
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Refines: [Rules applied, not written again](product.md#SharedRules)
- Applied by the obligation: [Its requirements held](sdlc.md#RequirementsServed)

<a id="Verified"></a>

### The code a shipment ships is verified

`Verified` · `src/obligations.ts:33` · status: **held**

Each scenario that verifies a node the shipment reaches, and each check whose program verifies one on a machine, is to prove. A reached node of the kinds named (entry points, functions…) that none of them verifies is a gap: a check made by hand is the family Checked's business, and proves nothing a machine can run.

<details><summary>The rule, in the code</summary>

```typescript
({ counts }) => (sketch: GraphSketch, reach: ObligationReach, p: { kinds: readonly string[] }): ObligationFinding => ({
    obliged: once(reach.reached.flatMap((r) => verifiedBy(sketch, r).map((s) => ({ node: s, via: r })))),
    gaps: reach.reached.filter((r) => p.kinds.some((k) => k === kindOf(sketch, r)) && counts.isEmpty(verifiedBy(sketch, r))),
  })
```

</details>

- Owner: trame
- Parameters: `counts` ← [Counts](algebra.md#Counts)
